title: Research: reduce selected P112 reader tariff to 81 (no κ change)
body:
## Summary

The selected gauge44 scatter has repeated centre-signature classes whose port labels are pairwise orthogonal. Pairing within those classes and completing the remaining labels gives a finite paired-plane decoder for the selected 112 ports.

A fixed-seed screen checks 500 matchings; all 500 admit an exact F2 factorization. The best sampled solution has four rank-one matrices, five rank-two matrices and 47 zero planes. Its raw port-support rank sum is 74. After closing source and reader supports under the complete matched planes, its algebraic complete-plane reader tariff is 81. Replaying the frozen predecessor under the same closure gives 144 (raw support-rank sum 126), a reduction of 63, or 7/16. The candidate passes the full decoder identity and all 28,672 exact endpoint inputs.

A separate exact basis change uses 104 integer row-add shears to localize the centre signal to eight anchor rows. The anchor readout has 20 nonzero coefficients; arbitrary residual consumption remains open.

## κ scope

No new selected κ is claimed. The selected result remains `0.001672660197076918`.

The exact favorable complex-side ceiling for the measured `{9:9}` profile and reader charge 81 is `0.005545369479` with two unpaid coordinates. It is `0.010103325422` with three unpaid coordinates, but the selected coverage law does not establish that third coordinate; the target relaxation margin is narrow (`0.9996848384694642`). A separate rank-16 idealization gives `0.012751469568` with two unpaid coordinates, but no such word is constructed. These are planning screens, not supplier or multiplication results. Native chronology, frames, dirty restoration, hosting, precision, cleanup, the bit-side contract and the complete supplier bill remain open.

## Validation

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/gauge44-port-syndrome-encoding --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/gauge44-port-syndrome-encoding
```

The registered standard-library replays pin the selected replay archive, canonical word, DATA-PHASES payload, predecessor certificate and ceiling engine. They check the rational scatter transform, 500 exact F2 factorizations and decoder identities, raw and complete-plane reader ranks, the frozen predecessor control, 28,672 endpoint cases and four exact ceiling screens.

## Overlap and credit

This extends the selected-port paired-plane work in Discussion #1587 and the existing paired-plane package. It optimizes a different finite decoder cost from PR #3335's plane-mask fitting rank. The complete-plane closure follows the reader distinction in PR #3398 and tariff in PR #3447; the unpaid-coordinate budgets are already screened in PR #3344. No priority over these predecessors is claimed. Prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no independent human review is claimed.
